workload: Two-word handle isolated from the object system. Genuine Rc<dyn Any> allocations of mixed concrete types, with 8-byte and 64-byte alignment. Equality and hashing use object identity. Handle<Base> traverses the valid offset-zero object prefix. Weak remains Weak<dyn Any>. All variants pass typed panic + exactly-once destruction, weak expiry, strong counts, upcast equality/hash, alignment and Option size checks.

modes.stock: Rc<dyn Any> with existing Rc::as_ptr address comparisons
modes.identity: Rc<dyn Any> with standard Rc::ptr_eq replacing only strong identity comparison
modes.raw: Two-word NonNull<dyn Any> from Rc::into_raw, stable raw count and reconstruction APIs. Weak creation takes a temporary extra strong via increment/from_raw.
modes.shared: Same data-first handle with out-of-line clone/drop.

build: rustc 1.99, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, opt-level=z, FatLTO, one codegen unit, unwind, safe ICF and RELR. Fixed fixture, unprofiled. 96 distinct typed getter, owned-read and identity-comparison leaves. The static fixture totals must not be extrapolated into the PGO shipping consumer.
method: Linux per-thread CPU clock on CPU 6. 61 seeded shuffled forward/reverse four-arm blocks after 3 warmups. Each process runs all five lanes; each lane uses 1,048,576 operations. Per-block average of two processes per arm, paired bootstrap of median ratios, 3,000 resamples, 95% interval. Lower ratios are faster.

sources.gen.py:
from pathlib import Path
d=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
def ty(i): return 'Align' if i%2 else 'Plain'
s=['#![allow(dead_code,unused_imports,private_interfaces)]','include!("core.rs");']
# Every slot is an externally addressable, concretely typed leaf that simulates a generated property
# accessor. A per-owner field and conversion constant force concrete distinct endpoints.
for n in range(96):
 t=f'{ty(n)}<{n}>'
 s += [f'#[no_mangle] pub fn read_{n}(x:&Handle<{t}>)->u64{{x.base.value.get().wrapping_add(x.extra[{n%3}]) ^ {n}}}',
       f'#[no_mangle] pub fn owned_{n}(x:&Handle<{t}>)->u64{{let y=black_box(x.clone());y.base.value.get().wrapping_add(y.extra[{n%3}]) ^ {n}}}',
       f'#[no_mangle] pub fn eq_{n}(x:&Handle<{t}>,y:&Handle<Base>)->usize{{if x.is_eq(y) {{{n+1}}} else {{0}}}}']
(d/'size.rs').write_text('\n'.join(s)+'\n')

shipping_alignment_signature.method: Match three consecutive decoded instructions in the shipping .text: mov reg,[base+0x10], dec same-reg, and same-reg,-16, fully within an identified function. This is the exact alignment idiom in the stock Ref fixture. Other Rust DST and layout operations also match, while spelling variations do not. These totals are signature measurements, not a byte saving or a complete census.

interpretation: The data-first strong handle reduces dereference and equality cost but moves the dynamic payload-to-header adjustment into reference counting. Its measured clone, upgrade and weak-round-trip regressions reject it for a parity build. Rc::ptr_eq alone keeps the standard carrier and shortens strong identity comparisons. Unchanged weak benchmark lanes differed across linked executable layouts; determine the overall cost from the integrated application. The production signature counts an instruction pattern and cannot be multiplied by the specimen or interpreted as exclusively Rc instructions.
reproduction: Write the sources entries side by side and run python3 gen.py. Build from that directory.
For each arm use no cfg for stock, --cfg identity, --cfg raw, or --cfg raw --cfg shared as named.
Build bench.rs with the same flags except --crate-type=cdylib. Run bench-$ARM qa and bench-$ARM SEED. Strip the size executable with GNU strip --strip-all -o size-$ARM.stripped size-$ARM.

Use nm -S -n on the unstripped libraries and count the unique physical intervals named read_[0-9]+, owned_[0-9]+, and eq_[0-9]+. Each array in the samples has the five lanes in listed order. The four shuffled arms run once forward then once in reverse order.

cold_receiver_projection.hypothesis: Keep Rc<dyn Any> and its normal reference counts. Call a shared out-of-line Rc::as_ptr only from cold reflection receiver projection; retain direct typed reads elsewhere. All three variants use the same standard Rc::ptr_eq identity check.
cold_receiver_projection.compiler: Same compact unprofiled FatLTO x86-64 Rust 1.99 flags and fixture as the parent report. A separate matched 61-block cohort on CPU 6 uses three arms in seeded shuffled forward/reverse order, 3 warmup blocks, seven lanes, 1,048,576 operations per lane. Paired median ratios have 95% bootstrap intervals, with 3,000 resamples.

arms.cold: 96 reflection leaves request shared_payload; ordinary Deref stays inline
arms.all_deref: Use shared_payload in all strong Deref and in reflection leaves

cold_receiver_projection.observed_codegen: For read_17, Rust/LLVM promotes the arguments to the noinline helper. The caller loads the owner and vtable, reads alignment at vtable+16, performs a call and adds stack adjustment. The 96 ordinary cold leaves consequently grow by three bytes each.
cold_receiver_projection.scope: The extra call is a measured negative for these 96 leaves. Unchanged lanes in separately linked tests may also shift through code layout. No global production size or speed delta follows.
cold_receiver_projection.reproduce: Generate original core.rs, size.rs and bench.rs from the parent sources in an original/ directory. Run this preparation source from its parent, then compile cold_projection/{size,bench}.rs with the same commands using --cfg identity for all variants, adding --cfg cold or --cfg all_deref as named.
